chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far (the second Imam, al-Baqir) (peace be upon him) along with some of our companions, and the reply came to me in his own handwriting. I said: 'You mentioned the matter of your daughter and her husband, may Allah rectify for you what you love to be rectified.' As for what you mentioned regarding his breaking his oath by divorcing her more than once, look (into the matter), may Allah have mercy on you. If he is among those who follow us and speak with our speech, there is no divorce upon him, because he did not do something he was ignorant of. And if he is among those who do not follow us nor speak with our speech, then effect an khula' (divorce by redemption) from him, for he only intended separation specifically.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّانَا: To follow us / be our follower
key_terms.يَقُولُ بِقَوْلِنَا: To speak with our speech (adhere to our rulings)

ai.seo_question: How does the Imam determine if multiple divorces are valid based on the husband's adherence to Shia teachings?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes the principle of 'Taqiyya' (dissimulation) in marital law, distinguishing between Shia men who conceal their knowledge of complex rulings to avoid burden and non-Shia men who divorce with simple intent. It clarifies that for those 'following us,' triple divorce does not take effect immediately if they feign ignorance, whereas for others, the divorce is valid based on their actual intention of separation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance where internal intent and external conformity to community norms interact to determine legal outcomes.
